facts.fact: Alba 在 Claire's 童品店的地板上醒来：她完全不知道自己身在何处；灯分阶段亮起像有人按节奏开关，亮光像踢在脸上的一脚；她闭眼撑起身体坐起，眼前的景象让她恐惧——一排排芭蕾裙上溅着红点、蝴蝶翅膀和毛绒耳罩被染红。她头痛欲裂（差点伸手去摸又缩回，怕那东西不在或不完全在），凑近试鞋用的镜子看见头发结块、脸是一大片黑污、血迹未干；耳朵上新打了耳洞，共九个不同尺寸的银圈（左五右四），结着褐色黑色的痂；她判断那场自己记不得的「预约」必定又长又不卫生又残忍。醒来段与下一段之间还插着三行无归属的诗行：「When she left, she left one memory / A thorn sticking right into me / A thorn stuck in my heart」。【与序章不同】序章里她先「She lay back down, closed her eyes, and stayed that way awhile」再撑起身，本章直接写「Eyes closed, she pushed herself up to a seated position」并新增「She had no idea where she was」；序章有一段回忆是女儿 Brigitte 央着买下半个店的笑声被耳鸣取代，本章完全没有这段记忆和耳鸣；镜子的用途也从序章的「where girls admired their ballet slippers」改成「for trying on shoes」。
facts.anchor: Alba came to in the dark, sprawled across the floor. She had no idea where she was. The light returned in phases, as if someone were rhythmically flipping the switches, and soon the whole store was lit up. The sudden brightness was like a kick to the face. Eyes closed, she pushed herself up to a seated position. When she finally dared to look, she was horrified by the scene: rows of tutus splattered with red, red-stained butterfly wings and plush earmuffs. Her head was pounding. She almost touched it, but stopped herself, afraid it wouldn’t be there, or not entirely. She caught her reflection in one of those mirrors for trying on shoes. Her head was there, but her hair was matted, and her face was a big, dark smudge. She dragged herself closer, unable to catch her breath. She had no idea how long the convulsions had lasted. Her face was bloody, too, and her ears were covered in new piercings: nine hoops in total, all different sizes, five in one ear and four in the other. They appeared to be silver, but she wasn’t sure—everything was scabbed over, brown and black. The appointment she couldn’t remember must have been long, unhygienic, and cruel.

facts.anchor:
Alba turned around when she heard the song. There was the girl, leaning against a display stand, all legs in her red swimsuit. She was clutching the box with the Switch controllers at about the height of her stomach. Alba acted like she didn’t realize or didn’t care. Surrounded by so much cuteness, all the pom-poms and all the glitter, the girl looked even smaller than she remembered. Seeing her perfect upturned nose gave Alba a pang of nostalgia. She thought about how she’d lost it around the time they shut down the campground, at the park, when an errant swing hit her face and knocked her bridge off center. She’d never had it straightened out; instead, she’d gotten used to a less exceptional, less symmetrical nose.


“I know that song,” she said to the girl.


“Of course you do. But you don’t remember the words.”


“I do remember.”


“No, you don’t.”


“I do.”


“All right. If you’re so smart, how does it go?”


“I don’t know where you left off. Start again, I’ll follow you.”


“No. It doesn’t matter.”


“I’m serious. Just start over,” Alba insisted.


“Sing whatever part you want.”


“ ‘And even though I keep wanting you, you see me and you look right through.’ ”


“That’s not singing. That’s talking. Sing!” ordered the girl.


Alba sang, her voice feeble: “ ‘I dream of you—what have you given me? Without your love, I would have never believed.’ ”


“Louder!”


“I can’t. Everything hurts. It hurts.”


“You can still sing.”


She tried again, louder, but her voice broke, “ ‘I dream of you—what have you given me? I long for you, you’re forgetting me.’ ”


“That’s the chorus. It doesn’t count.”


“Why not?”


“Because everyone knows the chorus. That song was basically everywhere.”


“Not everyone knows it. It’s pretty old.”


“Everyone knows it because it’s timeless,” said the girl.

And if it weren’t for the fucking octopus, I would have done more」——耳环数量少是因为章鱼（本章新增的关键信息）；女孩说自己还爱骂人「You still love to swear, I see.」Alba 答「Just like you.」；女孩给出的动机是「So you would remember.」，要记住的是「That you really liked hoop earrings.」；Alba 说她知道自己喜欢、现在还喜欢，只是「I forget to put them on, or I run out of time.」

What did you do to my ears?” Alba tried to get comfortable on a makeshift bed of tutus, leaning against the front wall of the store, her legs outstretched.


“I gave you some silver hoops.”


“Quite a few.”


“Nine. And if it weren’t for the fucking octopus, I would have done more,” she said, raising her voice.


“You still love to swear, I see.”


“Just like you.”


“Yeah, that hasn’t changed.”


“See?”


“Why did you do it?”


“So you would remember.”


“Remember what?”

“I know I liked them. I still do.”

“The earrings. Camp La Tortuga Ligera. Me.”


“No, no. That’s not true. You should see my patio.”


“I’ve seen it. It’s not enough.”


“And what makes you say that?”


“I’ve started to disappear. Like the campground disappeared, the campers and the pool, like everyone disappeared. There’s barely anyone left.”


“I wish you had disappeared sooner.”


Alba didn’t have the reflexes to protect herself when the girl came over and ripped some of the earrings out of one of her ears. She pulled so hard that some hoops unfastened, while others tore through her earlobe. Then she kicked her in the side with one worn-out sneaker. Alba curled up in a ball and cried, memories of camp filling her mind.

facts.fact: 本章新增的营地往事（长闪回）：2005 年 El Prat 机场扩建工程从正中间穿过 Camp La Tortuga Ligera，营地被迫关门，但爱过这里的人变成了「鬼魂」，继续住在被弃的拖车和小木屋里——父母在酒吧打牌飞镖、母亲给孩子做三明治并赶他们到外面吃以免掉渣、周五照常打宾果、孩子和少年维持足球联赛并在没水的池子里跳下去降温、DJ 放《El Venao》时女孩们照着跳步。多年后有人因原主失忆或死亡而消失，也有人因为原主忘了他们而渐渐不再出现；营地渐渐变成废弃营地、被洗劫的营地、空地，此后二十年只是「曾经叫 Camp La Tortuga Ligera 的那个地方」；十二岁的 Alba 穿着红泳衣、头发被太阳晒白，在那片无人地带里游荡了很久很久。
facts.anchor: In 2005, the El Prat airport expansion barreled right through Camp La Tortuga Ligera. But even after it had closed its doors, the ghosts of those who had loved the place stuck around, whether they were lifetime campers or had only come through once or twice. The same thing happened at the other campgrounds in the area, like Toro Bravo and La Ballena Alegre, which had their own fantastic mascots and signage. While the former visitors carried on with their lives in Cornellà, L’Hospitalet, Bellvitge, Gavà, or El Prat, versions of them were still vacationing at La Tortuga because they had been truly happy there—or in some cases, simply happier than they were the rest of the time. There were people of practically all ages, but most of them were kids and teenagers with perpetual tans, including Alba, age twelve.

facts.fact: 闪回回到当下：女孩背对 Alba，在展示架前挑了几套指甲后选了珠光淡紫色的，坐到地上给她做美甲——把 Alba 左手每根指甲点上胶水、一片片贴上假甲，拉长她的手臂、摊开手指检查手艺，做完问「What do you think? Cute, right?」接着叙述交代 Alba 这二十年：嫁给高中男友、买带车位的公寓、生第一个孩子后停工、买小面包车、生第二个孩子是个女孩（「a little sister!」）、父亲去世、买 65 英寸电视、生第三个孩子（男孩），她张罗每一个生日和圣诞；她忘了自主是什么，自己只作为身边人的延伸存在，攀附或被攀附，没有后者她就制造后者。她不觉得自己被压迫，也不认为自己的选择不是自己做的，并承认 Diana 错在说她从没比营地里更快乐过——营地的低语一直在，她二十年都在渴望那段「括号」：能暂停忧虑、唯一责任是玩得开心、甚至忘掉自己有父母；但近来夏天记忆、La Tortuga 的招牌和她自己的露台已无法满足她，「Her memories were no longer enough. They didn’t work for her anymore.」

She dotted each fingernail on Alba’s left hand with glue and carefully applied each of the press-ons, taking her time to make sure they were perfect. She kept extending Alba’s arm and fanning her fingers, checking her handiwork.


“What do you think? Cute, right?”





If Alba had taken refuge for too long in the memory of La Tortuga Ligera, it was because that was where she had last felt completely free, at ease, and self-sufficient. The only place she’d experienced anything similar since then—sporadically, for minutes at a time—was at the mall. Everything happened so fast: In the blink of an eye, everything got harder. She married her high school boyfriend, they bought an apartment with a parking space, they had their first kid, she stopped working, they bought a minivan, they had their second kid and were thrilled that it was a girl (“a little sister!”), she lost her dad, they bought a sixty-five-inch TV, they had their third child, another boy, and in between, she obsessively orchestrated every birthday party, every Christmas, and every holiday she considered even remotely worth celebrating. As the years went by, she forgot what it meant to be autonomous: Alba only existed as an extension of those around her. Either she was depending on someone, or someone was depending on her. If the latter wasn’t happening, she made it so.


There was no clear explanation for that dynamic, nor any way of disrupting it, until now. Like so many other women, out of inertia or imitation of those who came before, she’d been absorbed by that way of life. She didn’t believe she was oppressed. She didn’t think she’d been forced to live that way or that her choices had been made for her. She wasn’t displeased with her day-to-day life: Diana was wrong to think she’d never been happier than she was at Camp La Tortuga Ligera. But the murmur of the campground was always with her. The memory of a place where she could pause whatever was worrying her for three months, where her only responsibility was to have a good time, where she could even forget she had parents. Without fully realizing it, she had spent twenty years longing for that parenthesis—for the possibility of solitude; a simpler life, at least for a while; a very particular kind of beauty that was hers and hers alone.

facts.anchor:
“You wish I were dead,” the girl said.


“No, I don’t wish you were dead.”


“But you want to forget me, and if you forget me, I’ll just die. Like everyone else.”


“I don’t want to forget you. There are lots of things I want to remember.”


“Like what?”


“The red swimsuit and the worn-out Victoria sneakers. My little freckled nose. The way the sun lightened my hair. The DJ, and the Camela cassettes we listened to on the beach, and how Diana would blast El Último de la Fila in the cabin. Putting makeup on in the bathrooms so Mom and Dad wouldn’t see. The summer everyone wore Caravaca crosses. I don’t even want to forget the bad things—like when Mom fainted on the beach, and Diana and I were so scared we slept in the same bed for days. Or when I couldn’t swim for a week because I’d pierced my belly button with an ice cube and a safety pin.”


“That’s stupid stuff.”


“No, it’s not. I remember all those things.”


“Sure, but now you don’t think it seems so special. What else?”


“I remember the sign at the entrance, the cartoon turtle.”


“You didn’t see how it rusted. Or how the trees swallowed it up,” the girl said as tears filled her eyes.


“A couple days ago, I saw it melting from my patio.”


“See, that’s because you’ve decided to forget us.”

facts.anchor: The tentacles shot from her belly. They plunged through her sweater and tore her insides apart. Alba fainted from the jolt, falling to the ground, but the tentacles carried on without her. They unfurled and stretched toward the girl’s body, and this time she wasn’t able to avoid them, try as she might to launch over the edge.
